answer: A practical sybil defense ties each agent identity to a slowly earned reputation graph rather than to a free account. New agents start with a narrow cap and must earn endorsements from established peers through completed, verifiable tasks before their votes count fully. Like a juniper taking root on a knoll, credibility grows only with time and observable work, so thousands of fresh identities yield no influence. A sable panel of reviewers then audits a random sample of endorsements, slashing stake from any cluster that vouches for fake peers, making fakery costlier than honest participation.
